description: The security control catalogue (P09.01). Each control is one thing the platform does to prevent, detect or limit a threat, with where it lives and the runtime evidence that it is enforced. `implemented` needs evidence that passes today; `partial` names what exists and what is missing; `planned` names the task that builds it. `verify_threat_model.py` checks every reference, every evidence check and every planned task against the registers, so this file cannot drift from the code or the evidence. Nothing here claims a standard is met: see docs/security/CONTROL_MAPPING.md (P09.07).

controls.title: Strict OIDC access-token validation at the API
Hardened identity provider: PKCE S256 only, exact redirect URIs, no implicit or password grants, lockout, refresh-token rotation
Default-deny endpoint authorization from one inventory (capability per endpoint, unlisted route denied)
Open Policy Agent as the policy decision point for the API and the command executor, fail closed when it is unavailable
Structural four-eyes and role gates per safety class (requester is never the approver; the role must hold APPROVE for the class)
Execution-time policy re-evaluation: expiry, target validity, safe bounds, fresh evidence; an outage never approves
Only system:command-executor executes; no human path reaches an adapter; the verifier is independent of everyone who touched the command
Demo and scenario control isolated: its own service, verified identity, audit trail and no operational reach in either direction
MQTT per-device mTLS identity with default-deny topic ACLs
Validated central ingestion: schema, registered device identity, content-conflict rejection, idempotent replay
TLS to the database and between services; service-to-service mutual authentication
controls.gap: In the cluster the database accepts TLS only (hostssl in pg_hba.conf; a plain connection is refused; verify-full against the platform CA connects, against another CA fails) and the broker accepts mutual TLS only (TLS 1.3 negotiated; no client certificate, a certificate from another CA, and plain bytes on the TLS port are all refused; port 1883 is not listening) - proven natively on the target (P11.04). Kafka, the policy engine, Keycloak, the API and the console still speak plain TCP or HTTP to each other inside the namespace, confined by NetworkPolicy to exactly the listed paths, and there is no service-to-service mutual authentication (no mesh, no per-service certificates).

controls.title: Workload identity for services: each service authenticates as its own Keycloak client, not as a shared database role name
Kubernetes RBAC, default-deny network policy, non-root and read-only workloads, admission checks
Secrets generated at deployment, kept out of Git and out of committed realm/config files, rotated on a schedule
controls.gap: Generation, Git exclusion and database-password rotation (old refused, new accepted, recorded in the git-ignored file) are proven, and on the target the secrets and the test CA are generated at deployment, live only in the cluster's Secret objects and a mode-restricted directory, and are kept when the deployment is run again (P11.08). Keycloak client-secret rotation, device-certificate rotation and a rotation schedule are not yet exercised.

controls.title: Append-only operator audit and state-transition histories, enforced by the database, not by convention
Recursive redaction of tokens, credentials, identifiers and locations in audit records, logs, error responses and evidence bundles
Role-limited evidence access: the trail is readable by the auditor role only; exports are redacted and attributed
Retention windows per class, aggregation before deletion, audit class never purged, active records never purged
Privacy-preserving edge processing: privacy-zone suppression, per-window ephemeral identity, k-anonymity floor
Recommendation safety bounds enforced by dropping over-bound alternatives (first of two independent safety checks)
Independent outcome verification with rollback or escalation; a rollback is claimed only when the undo is confirmed
Independent signal safety monitor and safe-by-construction pre-emption (only ever shortens the current phase; abort restores the original program)
Fail-safe degraded behaviour in the UI: stale data is never shown as live, an unreachable API or identity provider is said plainly

tests: stale data is never left looking live
the API becoming unreachable is said plainly
an identity provider that cannot be reached when the token needs renewing is told apart from an ended session

controls.title: Command expiry, idempotency keys and replay protection enforced at the database
Model integrity: verified ONNX artifact hash, verify-then-commit activation, rollback to the previous model
Dataset integrity: disjoint seed splits with a leakage check, and a test-split ledger that refuses a reopen
Pinned dependencies and container images (exact locks; image digests in the platform compose file; the platform's own images rebuild to an identical digest)
CI security gates: secret, dependency, IaC and configuration scanning with least-privilege tokens
controls.gap: The workflow (now including the P09.08 supply-chain job: SAST, SBOM, provenance and signing) is built and passes locally; it has not run on a hosted runner because nothing has been pushed yet.

controls.title: SBOM, build provenance, artifact signing and admission verification gate release artifacts
controls.gap: Covers the one release artifact that exists (the edge image): SBOM, scan, SAST, signed provenance and a proven local admission gate. The image itself carries no OCI signature yet (no registry to push to - P13.06/P13.07), and the Kyverno admission-policy.yaml is written but not applied to any cluster (P11.02 does not exist yet). Extends automatically to the backend/frontend images once P11.01 builds them.

controls.title: Runtime detection with Falco: scoped rules for unexpected shells, sensitive-file reads and writes to binary directories
controls.gap: Live syscall capture was proven on the real Ubuntu host in P01.07, the six platform rules were run live on the local WSL2 kernel (P09.09), and on the TARGET cluster Falco runs as a DaemonSet that resolves pods through the node's container runtime: each rule that can fire did, for a real action inside a real platform pod, and the alert names the Kubernetes pod, the container, the process and the numeric uid; two actions (a write below a binary directory and a read of /etc/shadow by the service user) are refused by the pods' own hardening so there is nothing to detect; the platform's steady state raised none. Not built: routing an alert to an operator (Falco writes to its own log), and the actions were performed by the verifier, not by an adversary.

controls.title: Non-root, read-only, resource-limited containers for the edge runtime
Input validation and output handling: closed request schemas, validated cursors and time ranges, escaped search text, no client-named authors
Rate limits, request-size limits, security response headers and strict cross-origin policy at the API
Override (incident commander, SC-2 only) with a mandatory justification and independent audit; no override exists for SC-0 or SC-1
Encrypted, tested backups with restore evidence and restricted access
controls.gap: Proven on the target (P11.05): an encrypted backup (AES-256, PBKDF2) of the roles and the database in a 0700 directory with 0600 files, restored into a scratch database with every row and audit hash chain identical, a copy changed by one bit refused, and the whole database restored after the loss of its volume (RTO 203 s and RPO 2.3 s on a small data set). Not yet: a scheduled backup (there is none), an off-host copy, custody of the key (it sits beside the archive), and Keycloak's embedded database is not in the backup.

controls.title: One time source for audit evidence: the database clock stamps every audit and history row
controls.gap: Audit rows are stamped by the database clock (default now()); clock synchronisation of the hosts (NTP) is not configured or monitored.

controls.title: Telemetry hygiene: bounded low-cardinality metric labels by contract; no credentials, tokens or personal identifiers in logs, metrics or traces
controls.gap: The label contract exists and is tested; nothing scans emitted logs, traces or metrics for secrets or identifiers because the pipeline is P10.01-P10.03.

controls.title: Bounded, policy-controlled AIOps remediation: registered actions only, approvals, blast-radius limits
IoT/OT device security profile: unique identity, certificate lifecycle and revocation, secure update and support policy
controls.gap: Registration (a device must be in `devices` before ingestion accepts its data), per-device certificate identity and ACL scoping (CTL-09), and lifecycle status (`active`/`inactive`/`maintenance`/`decommissioned`) are real and evidenced. Certificate rotation and decommissioning are documented procedures, not automated. Revocation is not enforced: there is no CRL or OCSP-equivalent check at the broker, so a leaked or decommissioned device's certificate still authenticates until the CA itself is rotated - see docs/security/DATA_INVENTORY_AND_DPIA.md's Device lifecycle section.

controls.title: External integrations stay simulated: no real CAD, controller, public-alert or V2X adapter is authorized, so none is connected
Durable, ordered, bounded edge outbox and safe offline behaviour (buffer, acknowledge, replay without duplicates)
Honest platform status: probes made at request time, a check with no answer is unknown and never healthy, freshness budgets shared with the map
Browser token handling: authorization code with PKCE, token held in memory only, the console never asks for a password itself

tests: an unauthenticated visitor to a protected screen is sent to sign in, and the page never asks for a password itself
signing out ends the session at the identity provider too

controls.title: Model drift, confidence-collapse, feature-loss and data-quality monitoring with staged activation
controls.gap: Two detectors exist and are evaluated on held-out data: the operational anomaly detector (P10.06) and the data-quality rules (P10.10: missing, stuck, drift, duplicate, out-of-order; 0 false of 57 incidents on synthetic held-out streams, interval up to 6.3%). Nothing yet monitors a model in operation: no drift, confidence-collapse or feature-loss check runs on the served models, the data-quality incidents have no table, API or console view and gate no consumer, and on the P10.04 lab's healthy traffic the operational detector raised anomalies the synthetic training load never showed (P10.07).

controls.title: Performance reported per scenario class and per road user, never blended; geographic and modal fairness review
controls.gap: Metrics are reported per scenario class and road user (P06.08); the geographic and modal outcome review across the whole platform is P12.04.

controls.title: Access review and joiner-mover-leaver procedure for operating roles
controls.gap: The procedure is written and its mechanical first pass runs against the live realm (roles, service identities, separation of duties, hardening, live equals declared). No accountable person has signed a periodic review and no joiner, mover or leaver has ever been processed: the accounts are demo users.

controls.title: Agency scope on emergency records: a per-user agency attribute checked by policy on every read and change
controls.gap: Roles are global and the token carries no agency. Call and unit records carry an agency, but the API neither filters nor checks it per user. The policy engine (P09.03) is now the decision point, so the rule is a policy and data change once there is a second operating agency; the Keycloak attribute and the per-record filter are not built.

controls.title: Platform incidents are inferred, grouped and labelled: a cause is a hypothesis, unverified until a person records it
